rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning blessings particular to people, God follows with blessings particular to other creatures.
rows.anchor: لما بين ما يختص به الناس أتبعه بذكر ما يختص به غير الناس من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can bring forth grass; the idols worshipped by unbelievers cannot.
rows.anchor: هو القادر على إنبات العشب لا الأصنام التي عبدتها الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-marʿā encompasses vegetation the earth produces, including fruits, crops, and grasses.
rows.anchor: المرعى ما تخرجه الأرض من النبات ومن الثمار والزروع والحشيش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-marʿā as green herbage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المرعى الكلأ الأخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dried vegetation carried off by wadis and water and blown about by winds.
rows.anchor: الغثاء ما يبس من النبت فحملته الأودية والمياه وألوت به الرياح

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub gives ghuthāʾah as the singular form of ghuthāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب واحد الغثاء غثاءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawwah means blackness.
rows.anchor: الحوة السواد ، وقال بعضهم : الأحوى هو الذي يضرب إلى السواد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say aḥwā describes something that tends toward black when touched by moisture.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الأحوى هو الذي يضرب إلى السواد إذا أصابته رطوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first analysis, aḥwā describes the residue: pasture dries after being green and changes to black.
rows.anchor: أنه نعت الغثاء أي صار بعد الخضرة يابسا فتغير إلى السواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One cause of the blackening is cold drying the grass; cold whitens wet things and blackens dry ones.
rows.anchor: ومن شأن البرودة أنها تبيض الرطب وتسود اليابس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Floodwater can make the residue black by sticking muddy particles to it.
rows.anchor: أن يحملها السيل فيلصق بها أجزاء كدرة فتسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind can make the residue black by attaching abundant dust to it.
rows.anchor: أن يحملها الريح فتلصق بها الغبار الكثير فتسود

rows.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbaydah take aḥwā as black from the intensity of its greenness, like mudhāmmatān.
rows.anchor: اختيار الفراء وأبي عبيدة ، وهو أن يكون الأحوى هو الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative syntax makes the pasture first aḥwā and then ghuthāʾ, as in saying the Book was made upright and not crooked.
rows.anchor: والتقدير الذي أخرج المرعى أحوى فجعله غثاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yusrā means good works that lead to ease.
rows.anchor: اليسرى هي أعمال الخير التي تؤدي إلى اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred syntax coordinates this clause with 87:6 and treats 87:7 as an interjection; it means God will guide the Prophet to the easiest way of preserving the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says al-yusrā is Paradise, so God makes the Prophet able to do the deeds that lead to it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : اليسرى الجنة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God makes revelation easy for the Prophet to memorize, learn, and practice.
rows.anchor: نهون عليك الوحي حتى تحفظه وتعلمه وتعمل به

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God guides him to the easy, tolerant ḥanīfī law.
rows.anchor: نوفقك للشريعة وهي الحنيفية السهلة السمحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān and the Prophet say that the agent is made ready for an act, rather than the act being made easy for the agent; this wording also occurs in Sūrat al-Layl and the Prophetic saying.
rows.anchor: هذه العبارة كما أنها اختيار القرآن في هذا الموضع ، وفي سورة الليل

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet said, “Act; each person is facilitated for what he was created for.”
rows.anchor: اختيار الرسول في قوله عليه السلام : «اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An act is possible while existence and nonexistence remain equal; it occurs only when the active side is preferred, and that preference is facilitation, so the agent is made ready for the act.
rows.anchor: فإذا نرجح جانب الفاعلية على جانب التاركية ، فحينئذ يحصل الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majestic plural underscores the greatness of the gift through the greatness of its giver, as in other divine first-person plurals.
rows.anchor: إنما قال : { ونيسرك لليسرى } بنون التعظيم لتكون عظمة المعطى دالة على عظمة العطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God opened a degree of ease for the Prophet unequalled for anyone else, making an orphan raised among an ignorant people a model and guide for all humanity.
rows.anchor: فتح عليه من أبواب التيسير والتسهيل ما لم يفتحه على أحد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the Prophet through worldly and otherworldly benefits, God commands him to call people to truth and complete the deficient by reminding and guiding them.
rows.anchor: لما تكمل بتيسير جميع مصالح الدنيا والآخرة أمر بدعوة الخلق إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminder makes Muhammad a giver of perfection: one already complete becomes above-complete by completing others and guiding the ignorant.
rows.anchor: كان فياضا للكمال ، فكان تاما وفوق التمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A condition does not necessarily imply that the action is absent when its condition is absent; Qurʾānic examples include these five cases.
rows.anchor: أن المعلق بأن على الشيء لا يلزم أن يكون عدما عند عدم ذلك الشيء ، ويدل عليه آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation states the more compelling case: people are more strongly moved to act when they know the means will attain its goal.
rows.anchor: الصورة التي علم فيها إفضاء تلك الوسيلة إلى ذلك الغرض ، كان إلى ذلك الفعل أوجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation names the more exalted of two conditions while alluding to the other, meaning remind whether it benefits or not.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر أشرف الحالتين ، ونبه على الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation makes the condition an exhortation to benefit from the reminder and accept the truth.
rows.anchor: أن المراد منه البعث على الانتفاع بالذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation indirectly warns the Prophet that his audience is unlikely to respond, like asking someone to summon a person who may answer.
rows.anchor: يجري مجرى تنبيه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه لا تنفعهم الذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth explanation consoles the Prophet: repeated preaching increased their defiance and his grief, while repetition may be required only when success is hoped for.
rows.anchor: وكلما كانت دعوته أكثر كان عتوهم أكثر ، وكان عليه السلام يحترق حسرة على ذلك

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: A report says God told Moses to speak gently to Pharaoh, while witnessing that Pharaoh would not remember or fear; the duty to invite is distinct from divine knowledge of outcomes.
rows.anchor: كان يقول لموسى : { فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى } وأنا أشهد أنه لا يتذكر ولا يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The amount of reminding required is bounded by customary usage.
rows.anchor: أن الضابط فيه هو العرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fall into three groups about resurrection: those certain of it, those who consider it possible, and those who deny it; the first two can fear it.
rows.anchor: منهم من قطع بصحته ، ومنهم من جوز وجوده ولكنه غير قاطع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, the fearful person knows God’s power, knowledge, and wisdom and is certain of resurrection, as in the statement that only knowledgeable servants fear God.
rows.anchor: الذي يخشى هو الذي يكون عارفا بالله وعارفا بكمال قدرته وعلمه وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This identifies who benefits from the reminder; since only God can see inward fear, the Messenger must address everyone to reach those who will benefit.
rows.anchor: صفات القلوب مما لا اطلاع لأحد عليها إلا الله سبحانه وجب على الرسول تعميم الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On another reading, believers and non-hostile doubters fear; doubters are the majority, and together with the knowledgeable they greatly outnumber the hostile deniers.
rows.anchor: الخشية حاصلة للعاملين وللمتوقفين غير المعاندين وأكثر الخلق متوقفون غير معاندين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many adversaries resist only verbally; inwardly persistent deniers are exceedingly rare.
rows.anchor: فأما المعاند في قلبه بينه وبين نفسه فذلك مما لا يكون أو إن كان فهو في غاية الندرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warnings of the greater Fire and its condition of neither death nor life break hearts, so most people will listen and benefit; abandoning much good for little evil is itself a great evil.
rows.anchor: انكسر قلبه فلابد وأن يستمع وينتفع أغلب الخلق في أغلب الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although knowledge is usually called remembering only after it was acquired and forgotten, clear proofs make the knowledge seem already present and then removed by imitation and obstinacy.
rows.anchor: لقوة الدلائل وظهورها كأن ذلك العلم كان حاصلا ، ثم إنه زال بسبب التقليد والعناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle may express a promise whose fulfillment from God is certain, as in “We shall make you recite, and you will not forget.”
rows.anchor: السين في قوله : { سيذكر } يحتمل أن تكون بمعنى سوف يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the God-fearing person will remember after some time through reflection and deliberation.
rows.anchor: إن من خشي الله فإنه يتذكر وإن كان بعد حين بما يستعمله من التدبر والنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report identifies the verse’s occasion as ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت هذه الآية في عثمان بن عفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report identifies the verse’s occasion as Ibn Umm Maktūm.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في ابن أم مكتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the knowledgeable and non-hostile doubters fear and benefit from preaching, the most wretched is the hostile denier who refuses the call and avoids its reminder, entering the greater Fire.
rows.anchor: لابد وأن يكون لهما خوف وخشية ، وصاحب الخشية لابد وأن يستمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the damned neither die and find relief nor live a beneficial life; Arabs describe severe misery as being neither alive nor dead.
rows.anchor: لا يموت فيستريح ولا يحيا حياة تنفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the soul remains caught in the throat in Hell: it cannot leave and cause death or return to the body and restore life.
rows.anchor: أن نفس أحدهم في النار تصير في حلقه فلا تخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks this state as delayed because it is more dreadful and severe than entering the Fire.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه الحالة أفظع وأعظم من الصلى فهو متراخ عنه في مراتب الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading addresses the audience in the second person, supported by Ubayy’s written form.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة بالتاء ويؤكده حرف أبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second-person reading means that people prefer worldly deeds to deeds for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي بل أنتم تؤثرون عمل الدنيا على عمل الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says worldly food, drink, women, pleasures, and beauty are present and hastened, while the afterlife is unseen and deferred, so people choose the immediate.
rows.anchor: إن الدنيا أحضرت ، وعجل لنا طعامها وشرابها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb in the third person, meaning that the most wretched prefer worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو : ( يؤثرون ) بالياء يعني الأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever is better and more enduring deserves preference; the afterlife is therefore more deserving than the worldly life that people choose.
rows.anchor: أن كل ما كان خيرا وأبقى فهو آثر ، فيلزم أن تكون الآخرة آثر من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better because it contains both bodily and spiritual happiness, unlike worldly life.
rows.anchor: مشتملة على السعادة الجسمانية والروحانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly pleasures are mixed with pain, whereas the afterlife’s pleasures are not.
rows.anchor: أن الدنيا لذاتها مخلوطة بالآلام ، والآخرة ليست كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife lasts while the world perishes, and what endures is better than what perishes.
rows.anchor: أن الدنيا فانية ، والآخرة باقية ، والباقي خير من الفاني

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One view takes “this” to mean the whole sūra, which contains monotheism, prophethood, threats for unbelief, and promises for obedience.
rows.anchor: منهم من قال : جميع السورة ، وذلك لأن السورة مشتملة على التوحيد والنبوة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another view takes “this” to begin at 87:14: cleansing the theoretical faculty of false beliefs and the practical faculty of blameworthy traits.
rows.anchor: بل المشار إليه بهذه الإشارة هو من قوله : { قد أفلح من تزكى } إشارة إلى تطهير النفس

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: On this reading, remembering God completes the spirit through knowledge of Him, prayer adorns the limbs through obedience, worldly preference is censured, and the afterlife and God’s reward are encouraged.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله : { وذكر اسم ربه } فهو إشارة إلى تكميل الروح بمعرفة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The matters in this reading do not vary between religious laws, which explains why they were in earlier scriptures; Rāzī says reason and transmitted evidence support it.
rows.anchor: وهذه أمور لا يجوز أن تختلف باختلاف الشرائع ، فلهذا السبب قال : { إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى }

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr reports being asked whether the Qurʾān contains what is in Abraham’s and Moses’s scriptures and being told to read “Successful is whoever purifies himself.”
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي ذر أنه قال : قلت هل في الدنيا مما في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another group takes “this” to refer only to the nearest preceding statement, that the afterlife is better and more enduring.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : إن قوله { هذا } إشارة إلى قوله : { والآخرة خير وأبقى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to earlier scriptures is comparable to the Qurʾānic statements that it is in the earlier books and that God prescribed Noah’s religion.
rows.anchor: فهو نظير لقوله : { وإنه لفي زبر الأولين } وقوله : { شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical view makes “the scriptures of Abraham and Moses” an apposition explaining “the earlier scriptures.”
rows.anchor: أنه بيان لقوله : { في الصحف الأولى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the teaching is mentioned in the scriptures of all prophets, including those of Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: أن المراد أنه مذكور في صحف جميع الأنبياء التي منها صحف إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr reports that the Prophet counted 104 revealed books: ten to Adam, fifty to Seth, thirty to Idrīs, ten to Abraham, then the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Furqān.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي ذر أنه سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كم أنزل الله من كتاب ؟

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A report says Abraham’s scriptures taught that a wise person should guard his tongue, know his time, and attend to his own affairs.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن في صحف إبراهيم : ينبغي للعاقل أن يكون حافظا للسانه عارفا بزمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting proofs for monotheism and resurrection, God tells the Messenger to remind people with these and similar proofs, urging reflection and warning against neglect.
rows.anchor: على صحة التوحيد والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger was sent for the work of reminding and must patiently endure whatever obstacles accompany it.
rows.anchor: وذلك بعث منه تعالى للرسول على التذكير والصبر على كل عارض معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the unbeliever asks whether anyone saw him, God adduces the human organs as evidence of His complete power.
rows.anchor: لما حكى عن ذلك الكافر قوله { أيحسب أن لم يره أحد } أقام الدلالة

rows.speaker: أهل العربية
rows.claim: Arabic linguists define najd as a road rising upward.
rows.anchor: قال أهل العربية : النجد الطريق في ارتفاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because proofs are clear, they are likened to a raised road that is conspicuous to sight; most exegetes therefore take the two roads as good and evil.
rows.anchor: لما وضحت الدلائل جعلت كالطريق المرتفعة العالية بسبب أنها واضحة للعقول

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s explanation that the two paths are good and evil, and that no one should prefer the evil path to the good.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أنه عليه السلام قال : «إنما هما النجدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance here parallels the statement that God guided the human being to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية كالآية في : { هل أتى على الإنسان } إلى قوله : { فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan relates the question of who would reckon with the person boasting “I have squandered heaps of wealth”; the answer is the one able to create his organs.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : قال { أهلكت مالا لبدا } فمن الذي يحاسبني عليه ؟

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab identify the two paths as the breasts, routes to the child’s life and provision; God guides infants to nurse.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب ، أنهما الثديان

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl prefers the first interpretation, the two paths of good and evil.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : والتأويل هو الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator of an intelligent heart and articulate tongue from lowly fluid can destroy what He made and knows its secrets; clear proofs and evident favors leave no excuse for disbelief or arrogant spending against God and His supporters.
rows.anchor: إن من قدر على أن يخلق من الماء المهين قلبا عقولا ولسانا قؤولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If nafs means the body, its fashioning is the proportioning of its limbs, as anatomy shows.
rows.anchor: إن حملنا النفس على الجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If nafs means the governing faculty, its fashioning is by giving it powers of hearing, sight, imagination, thought, and memory, as psychology shows.
rows.anchor: فتسويتها إعطاؤها القوى الكثيرة كالقوة السامعة والباصرة والمخيلة والمفكرة والمذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the indefinite noun is that it singles out the prophetic, sanctified soul as chief over the world of composite beings.
rows.anchor: أن يريد به نفسا خاصة من بين النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This view reasons that every multiplicity has a chief: composites are headed by animals, animal kinds by humans, human kinds by prophets, and the prophets by one supreme leader.
rows.anchor: كل كثرة ، فلابد فيها من واحد يكون هو الرئيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite noun means every soul and conveys abundance, as in “each soul shall know what it has brought.”
rows.anchor: أن يريد كل نفس ، ويكون المراد من التنكير التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Souls belong to innumerable animal kinds; each is distinct in its defining qualities, and human understanding cannot grasp even the few qualities of fleas and mosquitoes, much less God’s secrets.
rows.anchor: ولكل نوع نفس مخصوصة متميزة عن سائرها بالفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says inspiration means making the soul understand wickedness and piety, know which is good or bad, and enabling it to choose; it parallels the two paths in 90:10.
rows.anchor: أن إلهام الفجور والتقوى ، إفهامها وإعقالهما

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: This interpretation accords with the Muʿtazilite doctrine.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل مطابق لمذاهب المعتزلة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites cite the following verse about success through purification as support for their interpretation.
rows.anchor: قالوا : ويدل عليه قوله بعد ذلك : { قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The understanding-and-choice interpretation is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and a group of eminent exegetes.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه مروي عن ابن عباس وعن جمع من أكابر المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says God inspires the believer with piety and the unbeliever with wickedness.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى ألهم المؤمن المتقي تقواه وألهم الكافر فجوره

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr glosses the phrase as God imposing its wickedness and piety upon the soul.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير : ألزمها فجورها وتقواها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God placed these qualities in the soul by granting it success in piety and abandoning it to wickedness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد : جعل فيها ذلك بتوفيقه إياها للتقوى وخذلانه إياها بالفجور

rows.speaker: الزجاج والواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj and al-Wāḥidī choose the second interpretation.
rows.anchor: واختار الزجاج والواحدي ذلك

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī distinguishes inspiration from teaching and clarification: it is God’s placing something in the servant’s heart, thereby imposing it.
rows.anchor: فإن الإلهام هو أن يوقع الله في قلب العبد شيئا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī traces ilhām to laham, to swallow or consume, and says inspiring is like delivering something into the heart.
rows.anchor: وأصل معنى الإلهام من قولهم : لهم الشيء

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says Ibn Zayd’s gloss best fits the root sense and plainly means God creates piety in the believer and wickedness in the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: فالتفسير الموافق لهذا الأصل قول ابن زيد ، وهو صريح في أن الله تعالى خلق في المؤمن تقواه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء وعكرمة ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They interpret the next verse to mean that the soul God purified, rectified, and cleansed prospered, that is, God enabled it to obey.
rows.anchor: قد أفلحت وسعدت نفس زكاها الله تعالى وأصلحها وطهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier oaths established God’s governance of the simple and composite celestial and terrestrial bodies; inspiration now addresses the remaining question of whether voluntary animal acts also fall under His decree.
rows.anchor: أن الآيات الثلاثة ذكرت للدلالة على كونه سبحانه مدبرا للأجسام العلوية والسفلية البسيطة والمركبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that voluntary acts also come from God and His decree; everything besides God occurs under His creation and control.
rows.anchor: بقوله : { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها } على أن ذلك أيضا منه وبه وبقضائه وقدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choices must arise from an agent: if causeless, an originated thing has no maker; if caused by the servant, regress follows; if caused by God, the intended conclusion follows.
rows.anchor: فحصولها إن كان لا عن فاعل فقد استغنى المحدث عن الفاعل ، وفيه نفي الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Introspection confirms this: an unbidden thought enters the heart, produces inclination, then bodily movement and action, proving that inspiration means divine enabling or abandonment.
rows.anchor: فتقع صورته في قلبه دفعة ، ويترتب على وقوع تلك الصورة في القلب ميل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya means purification or growth.
rows.anchor: التزكية عبارة عن التطهير أو عن الإنماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the person succeeds by purifying their own soul from sins through obedience and avoiding disobedience.
rows.anchor: أنه قد أدرك مطلوبه من زكى نفسه بأن طهرها من الذنوب بفعل الطاعة ومجانبة المعصية

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī accepts the alternative that God purifies the soul, taking this as God judging and naming it pure in ordinary usage.
rows.anchor: وقبل القاضي هذا التأويل ، وقال المراد منه أن الله حكم بتزكيتها وسماها بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-purification reading initially seems nearer because “soul” was stated explicitly, while the alternative refers to something only understood as mentioned.
rows.anchor: والأول أقرب ، لأن ذكر النفس قد تقدم ظاهرا ، فرد الضمير عليه أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because 91:8 was shown to mean that God grants piety and abandons the wicked, this verse must likewise mean that God purifies the soul.
rows.anchor: أن المراد ، بألهمها ما ذكرناه فوجب حمل اللفظ عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī’s interpretation as mere divine judgment or naming is weak: the verb form denotes bringing about, and a divine judgment cannot change without making truth false and knowledge ignorance.
rows.anchor: لأن بناء التفعيلات على التكوين ، ثم إن سلمنا ذلك لكن ما حكم الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun should return to the nearer antecedent: the mention of “inspiring it” is nearer than “a soul,” supporting the interpretation just given.
rows.anchor: فإن أهل اللغة اتفقوا على أن عود الضمير إلى الأقرب أولى من عوده إلى الأبعد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن أبي هلال
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Abī Hilāl reports that the Prophet paused when reciting this verse and prayed for his soul’s piety and purification, saying God is its guardian and the best to purify it.
rows.anchor: ما رواه الواحدي في البسيط عن سعيد بن أبي هلال أنه عليه السلام كان إذا قرأ
